title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. X is a smooth proper connected curve of genus g >= 2. A projective connection c on X gives a rank-2 bundle E with a connection, defined up to twist; in modern terms this is the PGL2-oper. E is the non-split extension 0 -> ω_X -> E -> O_X -> 0, so det E ≃ ω_X. The 'G-fibré' is the PGL2-torsor P(E) together with its flat structure; here G denotes horizontality, i.e. compatibility with the connection or stratification.

Previous page. Grothendieck shows that the map u_ω: c -> c + d^1(ω) separates projective connections. He then asks whether the associated G-bundle has automorphisms. An automorphism would force a horizontal reduction of structure group to a Borel subgroup. Concretely, P(E) ≃ P(F) with E ≃ F⊗L, where F is a horizontal extension 0 -> M -> F -> O_X -> 0 and M is an invertible sheaf with connection.

This page. The aim is to rule out such a Borel reduction.
(1) Degree of L. Taking determinants gives ω_X ≃ det E ≃ det F ⊗ L^2 = M ⊗ L^2. Since M carries a connection, deg M = 0 in characteristic 0. Hence 2 deg L = 2g-2, i.e. deg L = g-1.
(2) The composite ω_X -> E ≃ F⊗L ->> L. This is a section of L⊗ω^{-1}, which has degree (g-1)-(2g-2) = -(g-1) < 0, so the composite vanishes.
(3) Hence E ->> L factors through E/ω_X ≃ O_X. This gives a surjection O_X ->> L, so L ≃ O_X. That contradicts deg L = g-1 ≠ 0. So no horizontal Borel reduction exists.
(4) Normalizer of a torus. Suppose the structure group reduces to the normalizer N(T) of a maximal torus. The induced étale double cover X' of X has genus >= 2, and the pulled-back projective connection reduces to T, hence to a Borel. This contradicts step (3) applied on X'. The same device handles finite subgroups (a finite étale cover trivializes the bundle).
(5) Theorem stated. For X of genus >= 2 over k (char 0 '?'), the PGL(2)-torsor attached to any projective connection admits no horizontal reduction to a proper closed subgroup H' ⊊ PGL2. The next page translates this for k = C: the monodromy π1(X,x) -> PGL2(C) has Zariski-dense image. Equivalently, the differential Galois group of every PGL2-oper on a curve of genus >= 2 is all of PGL2.

This also answers the automorphism question: automorphisms of the flat torsor correspond to the centralizer of the monodromy, which is trivial for a Zariski-dense subgroup.
errors: The transcription's 'ω^{-1} -> E' should be the subbundle ω_X -> E. The section lies in Hom(ω, L) = L⊗ω^{-1}, of degree -(g-1). The argument is correct with this reading.

The step deg M = 0 holds because M carries a connection, which is valid only in characteristic 0. In characteristic p a line bundle with connection only has degree divisible by p, so step (1) breaks. Grothendieck's hesitation '(de car. nulle ?)' is therefore justified: the argument as written needs char 0, and in char p the statement must be reformulated (e.g. for dormant opers, via the Cartier descent W of F^*W).

The classification of proper closed subgroups of PGL2 is used implicitly: subgroups of a Borel, subgroups of N(T), finite subgroups. The finite and toral cases are dispatched only by the brief 'même argument' via étale covers. This is fine but only sketched.
Minor: in step (3), surjectivity of O_X -> L (needed to conclude L ≃ O_X) follows from surjectivity of E -> L; this is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: No horizontal Borel reduction of the PGL2-bundle of a projective connection, via the degree computation deg L = g-1 and the vanishing of Hom(ω, L)
ideas.modern_name: Irreducibility of oper monodromy / opers are not reducible (the Hodge-filtration line ω ⊂ E is 'maximally destabilizing')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, holonomy of projective structures is irreducible); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s)

ideas.what: Normalizer-of-torus case reduced to torus case via an étale double cover, with genus >= 2 preserved
ideas.modern_name: Standard étale-cover reduction in differential Galois group / monodromy arguments

ideas.what: Theorem: the monodromy (differential Galois group) of any projective connection on a curve of genus >= 2 is Zariski dense in PGL2 (equal to PGL2)
ideas.modern_name: Zariski density / non-elementarity of holonomy of complex projective structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning 1967; Gallo–Kapovich–Marden 2000 (non-elementary holonomy); algebraic oper version folklore

ideas.what: Absence of automorphisms of the flat PGL2-torsor attached to a projective connection
ideas.modern_name: Opers have trivial automorphism group (the oper locus is a section of the de Rham stack, schematic)

missed.claim: A purely algebraic, characteristic-0 proof (by degree count and étale covers) that the monodromy of every projective connection on a curve of genus >= 2 is Zariski dense in PGL2. Grothendieck explicitly flags the characteristic assumption as doubtful. That is precisely the point where the char-p theory (dormant opers, p-curvature) diverges, though he does not pursue it.
missed.quote: Th. Soit X courbe projective lisse et connexe de genre g≥2 sur corps k (de car. nulle ?). Alors pour toute connexion projective sur X, on ne peut pas réduire le groupe structural ... à un sous-groupe H' distinct de H
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck was treating projective connections (opers) algebraically, in a relative setting over S, before Beilinson–Drinfeld. The result itself is known (Gunning; Gallo–Kapovich–Marden), so it is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard argument, and the result is known: oper/projective-structure monodromy is irreducible and Zariski dense. The only interest is historical, as an algebraic oper-style treatment with a flagged characteristic-p caveat.
transcription_corrections: 'ω^{-1} -> E ≃ F⊗L ->> L' should read 'ω_X -> E ≃ F⊗L ->> L' (ω_X as the subbundle of E).
'[-faisceau-] {+groupe+} structural des G-fibrés projectifs associé à une connexion projective' is confirmed as written.
Second line: under 'det E' and 'det F' are written ω_X and M respectively, i.e. ω_X ≃ M⊗L^{⊗2}.
